messages.author: d5b22c2be9055ac8
messages.subject: Line Transect effort and global detection function
parts:
Hello List:
In my experiment, I surveyed birds on 12 treatment areas. Each treatment area had one survey route and each route was completed 7 times each year for 3 years. I would like to calculate densities of 8 species on each route for each year, with observer as a covariate. I am using the MCDS engine. Here's my question: How do I obtain global detection functions for each species, pooling all observations from all transects across all years, and use that information to get density estimates for each transect.

I know that effort needs to be 7x the line length for a given year. One method I have tried is to set my data filter for species only. Then, in my model, I have selected all the observations (for a given species) for a year and post-stratified by each transect, yielding 12 density estimates total - one per transect. However, when I do that, the effort is not correct, so obviously the density is also wrong. In fact, I'm not even sure how effort is calculated in this case. Is this a simple matter of scaling the calculated density by the ratio of the effort (line length) used in the model by the actual line length x 7?

Is there a way to calculate a global detection function for each species, then apply that to a dataset filtered for species, compartment, and year?

This seems like a basic operation, but I can't seem to figure out how to do it.

Thanks for any suggestions.

Todd Plummer

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Line Transect effort and global detection function
parts:
Hi Todd, list:

How about the following: set up the project with one record in the sample layer
for each route in each year -- ie 12x3=36 records. For each record, effort is 7x
line length for the given year. Observer is a field at the appropriate level
(sample if the same observer did all 7 repeats of a line, or observation if not.)
You also need species as a field in the observation layer. Set up a data filter
for each species. Set up a model definition with detection function global and
encounter rate and density by sample. Should give you what you want.

Note that the sample density estimates will not be independent, because they share
some parameters in the detection function. You'll need to take this into account
if you want to get variances on comparisons of densities across years or treatment
areas (unless they share the same observer, in which case you're effectively just
comparing encounter rates). Probably conceptually the simplest way to do this is
to bootstrap the comparison. E.g., if you want to compare density in the first
and last year then calculate the difference in density, draw a bootstrap resample
from your data (at whatever level is appropriate -- are treatment areas the random
thing here?), refit the data in Distance (probably calling the MCDS engine
directly from whatever program you use to do the bootstrap) calculate a new
difference, repeat many times and this gives you and estimate of the distribution
of the differences. Downside is that you have to program in some language to do
this.

Finally, thanks for sending me your project file (under separate cover) - I hope
the above answers your questions. However, can I please implore everyone who
wants to send a project file to me to export it as a zip file first -- read the
online manual, Chapter 4 for details.

Cheers,

- Len
